audit.why: 51.27% over 1024 games; LeBlanc owns levels 1 through first item and Neeko flips it in grouped fights. Chart (LeBlanc x6, Neeko at 2+ items) agrees with the packet and with both layers.
Neeko's spike is Pop Blossom at 6 (120s at rank 1, 90s at rank 3) and grouped fights late; LeBlanc's is 2, 6 and first item. Already reflected.
audit.corrected: spikes[1] tightened to name the hidden wind-up rather than a vague 'channel'.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer attributed the root to Blooming Burst (Q). Blooming Burst is the seed poke; the root is Tangle-Barbs (E), 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s at 1000 range. The page also told you to sidestep the root 'behind minions'.
audit.why: Tangle-Barbs damages and roots everything it passes through and becomes larger, faster and longer-rooting after passing a champion — minions do not block it, and hiding in the wave is actively wrong advice. Separately, Pop Blossom's preparation is hidden while Inherent Glamour is active, which is the real trap at 6.
audit.corrected: Root reattributed to Tangle-Barbs everywhere, pass-through behaviour stated, hidden Pop Blossom wind-up added.

audit.why: Tangle-Barbs' 12s-to-10s window is the only clock this lane runs on.

edits.before: Neeko's kit revolves around landing Blooming Burst for a root, which is her only real way to punish your engage — everything else is reactive poke and passive farming. Bait that root with the wraith clone, since she has no dash or blink to save herself once it's spent, and then all-in with your real body for a clean kill. Her damage in isolated trades is mediocre compared to your burst combo, so as long as you play patiently around her root cooldown you win almost every early skirmish.
edits.after: Neeko's kit revolves around landing Tangle-Barbs (E) — Blooming Burst (Q) is the seed poke, the tangle is the root, and it passes through the whole wave on a 12-second cooldown, so standing behind minions saves you from nothing. Sidestep it, or eat it on the Mirror Image, since she has no dash or blink to save herself once it is spent, then all-in with your real body. Play around that one cooldown and you win almost every early skirmish.

edits.before: At 6 your full combo still kills her outright before Pop Blossom can channel, provided you engage from outside her root's threat range and don't let her set up first. Her ultimate is primarily a teamfight tool — a channeled stun bomb — so in a straight 1v1 it does very little for her unless you let her land the setup root beforehand. Keep pressuring and roaming; Neeko has no way to punish your rotations since her disguise trick works best with allied backup, which she won't have in a 1v1 lane.
edits.after: At 6 your full combo still kills her outright before Pop Blossom lands, provided you open from outside the 1000-range tangle and don't let her set up first. The ultimate knocks up on the leap and stuns on the landing inside 600 range, so in a straight 1v1 it does little for her unless the root goes in first. Keep pressuring and roaming, but respect the disguise on rotations: Inherent Glamour hides the Pop Blossom preparation, and the ally you walk past may be her.

notes: packet.suspectNames flagged "Pop Blossom's" in whys[6] as a probable wrong name — false positive, that is the correct ability with a possessive. The real name error was the opposite direction: the content layer called Blooming Burst (Q) a root when the root is Tangle-Barbs (E). Also removed the 'sidestep it behind minions' advice, which is backwards — Tangle-Barbs roots everything it passes through and grows after hitting a champion. Chart left untouched.
